outcome: Presence of SARS-CoV-2 in amniotic fluid
Presence of SARS-CoV-2 in cord blood
Presence of SARS-CoV-2 in neonatal nasopharyngeal swabs
cohort: The study included 44 pregnant women (43 with singleton pregnancies and one with a twin pregnancy) diagnosed with COVID-19 during pregnancy.
finding: Mother-to-child transmission of SARS-CoV-2 is possible but uncommon, as indicated by the presence of the virus in placenta, amniotic fluid, and cord blood, and a positive neonatal nasopharyngeal swab in one case at 24-48 hours.
followup_time: Up to 48 hours after birth for neonatal nasopharyngeal swabs
cross-section timing: Samples taken immediately after birth and neonatal swabs repeated at 24-48 hours after birth.
gest_age: Median gestational age at maternal diagnosis was 34.7 weeks (range 14-41.3 weeks).
